headline: Revenue accelerates, one-time charge hits GAAP earnings

kpis.label: GAAP gross margin on net product sales

summary_short: Regeneron's Q2 2026 revenue rose 17% y/y to $4.29 billion, but GAAP net income fell 7% to $1.30 billion and diluted EPS fell 5% to $12.23, weighed by a $127 million acquired IPR&D charge that cut GAAP and non-GAAP EPS by roughly $1.00 and $0.99 per share, respectively.
summary_long: Revenue rose 17% y/y to $4,291M, led by 38% Dupixent growth (Sanofi-recorded), 52% U.S. EYLEA HD growth, and 30% Libtayo growth, partly offset by EYLEA's 45% decline as patients shift to EYLEA HD. GAAP net income fell 7% to $1,297M and diluted EPS fell 5% to $12.23, driven by a $127M acquired IPR&D charge (~$1.00/share) and a GAAP gross margin decline to 78% from 83% on a since-resolved Limerick, Ireland manufacturing interruption. The Sanofi Development Balance was fully repaid at quarter-end. Cash fell to $2,456M on $1.2B of buybacks; long-term debt was flat near $1,987M. Regeneron narrowed FY2026 GAAP R&D guidance to $6.50-$6.635B and raised gross-margin guidance to 78-79%.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by 38% global Dupixent net sales growth (Sanofi-recorded), 52% U.S. EYLEA HD growth, and 30% global Libtayo growth, partly offset by a 45% EYLEA decline as patients transition to EYLEA HD.
Reflects the $127M acquired IPR&D charge and a lower GAAP gross margin on net product sales (78% vs 83%) from the Limerick manufacturing interruption, partly offset by 17% revenue growth.
The release states the $127M acquired IPR&D charge cut GAAP diluted EPS by approximately $1.00 per share this quarter.
Tracks the diluted EPS decline; basic (102.8M) and diluted (106.0M) weighted-average shares move together this quarter.
Grew despite the IPR&D charge (which also cut non-GAAP EPS by about $0.99/share) because non-GAAP net income excludes stock-based comp, intangible amortization, and manufacturing-interruption costs.
Total revenue grew 17% while total GAAP operating expenses (per Table 2) grew a smaller 15%, so operating income grew faster than revenue despite the IPR&D charge.

drivers.metric: GAAP gross margin on net product sales
drivers.explanation: The release attributes the decline from 83% to 78% to unabsorbed manufacturing costs from a temporary bulk-manufacturing interruption at the Limerick, Ireland facility, which had returned to normal by quarter-end.
Computed as total revenue less COGS and cost of collaboration/contract manufacturing; grew because revenue (+17%) outpaced the combined ~9% growth in COGS plus COCM.
Operating income rose on revenue growth, but other income (expense) fell to $234.3M from $439.2M on lower net gains on marketable securities, roughly offsetting the operating-income gain.
The q/q decline from $2,962.6M is largely explained by the disclosed $1.2B of Q2 share repurchases; the y/y increase reflects cumulative profit generation, not separately narrated in the release.
Not explained in the release; the balance is essentially unchanged q/q and y/y with no new financing activity disclosed this quarter.
Increase driven primarily by $1,296.9M of net income for the quarter, partly offset by the $1.2B of share repurchases disclosed in the Capital Allocation section.
Reflects the ongoing share-repurchase program; the release discloses $2.0B of YTD (six-month) buybacks reducing the diluted share count from 108.6M a year ago.

CEO Leonard Schleifer cited 'strong financial performance' from commercial-portfolio strength and the ~50-asset pipeline; CFO Christopher Fenimore highlighted full repayment of the Sanofi Development Balance, which will lift collaboration profits starting Q3.
